evidence: The hunk shows `!candidate.Present()` removed from `contestants()`, which opens a new path (public checkout as contestant). The only existing test the reviewer names covers the reverse direction. The agent added `TestPublicCheckoutContestsAnIdentifiedHolder` and mutation-checked it against restoring the filter.
guidance_note: When a change removes a filter from a symmetric relation, write the test for each direction the removal newly allows before opening the PR.

evidence: The agent confirmed that every standing literal in claims_render_test.go uses a non-zero Attribution, so the three new renderings are never reached. It deleted the self-match branch instead of pinning it, because F3/F7 showed the branch was wrong, and then tested the corrected rendering (`TestFormatClaimLinePublicCheckoutIsNeverHere`) and the describeClaimant branches.
guidance_note: Every new user-facing string branch a PR adds needs a rendering test that reaches it; a grep for the literal finding only its definition is the pre-PR check.

evidence: The agent verified that `reportContestedLanes` builds `&app.App{Workspace: ws, Store: syncStore}` with no Stream, so `cc.self` is always zero and the branch `!by.Present() && by == cc.self` would claim a foreign public hold as "here". The plan said the render would carry whether a self identity exists. The landed fix (edb1a45) deleted the branch instead. F10 later established that an unminted checkout never records events in production, so deleting it was the sounder fix.
guidance_note: Before letting a zero value mean 'this is me', list every caller that builds the context and check that each one can actually supply a self identity.

evidence: This repeats F2 in round 1, raised at 19:20 before the agent's first replies at 19:24, so no fix existed yet to cause it. The test gap was real (the reviewer's grep for "no stream token minted" found only the definition). The agent correctly declined to pin a branch it was deleting and tested the replacement rule.

The agent verified the regression with line refs (`next` is AccessRead; ReadStream never mints; relationOf matches Stale by equality). The reviewer's first fix direction was 'only apply the self-is-public-checkout match once this checkout has minted its own token'. The agent narrowed that to the Stale arm only and argued a fresh public hold is still the checkout's own. F10 showed this was false in production, and 8a17449 extended `self.Present()` to the Held arm, which is the reviewer's original suggestion.
guidance_note: When the root cause is 'equality of an unaddressable identity is taken as ownership', apply the fix at every arm that compares by that equality, not only the arm in the reproduced scenario.

evidence: describeClaimant's empty-assignee branch returns `nameCheckout(c.Checkout)` (shown in the hunk), and every transfer-notice e2e test went through app.Open, which mints a token. guidance_note: When a PR replaces an existing user-facing string, add a test asserting the new string on the path that produces it before review.

evidence: The reviewer's trace holds: the App literal in reportContestedLanes has no Stream, so ownAttribution collapses to zero and the branch prints false self-attribution. The agent's plan proposed a type that distinguishes 'no self' from 'self is public', but edb1a45 deleted the branch instead. That still removes the conflation the cited law targets, and F10's analysis shows no unminted checkout owns public holds anyway.
guidance_note: When a sentinel value takes on a new meaning, enumerate the meanings it already carries (pre-attribution, unminted, no identity available) and give each one a distinct representation before you write a branch on it.

evidence: F5's fix (edb1a45/3c30e79) narrowed the rule to fresh holds and rewrote the cold-start paragraph and the CHANGELOG. It left the vocabulary paragraph saying unqualified that an unminted checkout 'holds what it worked and is served out of it'. 68e3b16 added the freshness qualifier and pointer, and the agent swept the rest of the doc.
guidance_note: When a fix narrows a documented rule, grep the doc and changelog for every statement of that rule in the same commit, rather than only the paragraph the finding cited.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The named commit 68e3b16 changed only design-docs/work-claims.md, and the derive.go leg-2 comment ('Exactly one way ... no lifecycle transition ever happened') is a rewrite of the base 'Two ways' text that went unflagged in earlier rounds. The packet does not show it coming from any fix commit. The reviewer is right that leg 4's local.Void can empty `admissible`. The agent conceded this and rewrote the comment to 'with none left, nobody holds the lane'.
guidance_note: Before writing 'exactly one way' in a comment, trace every path into the branch, including filters applied upstream such as leg 4's voiding.

evidence: F5's fix added `self.Present()` to relationOf's Stale arm only and wrote the cold-start sentence 'fresh unattributed evidence is evidence this checkout produced itself'. 68e3b16 then repeated that freshness carve-out in the vocabulary paragraph. The agent checked the premise further: app.Open mints a token before any write, so an unminted checkout has recorded nothing and a fresh public hold is never its own. In 8a17449 it guarded the Held arm too, made the harness mint through app.New, and inverted the test.
guidance_note: Before keeping a carve-out such as 'a fresh public hold is still yours', verify which production write path could have produced that evidence; here app.Open's minting rules it out.

narrative: The PR made unattributed work belong to a shared 'public checkout' and let an unminted checkout recognize public holds as its own. Rounds 0-1 found the missing tests, a false self-attribution on Stream-less callers (F3/F7), and the headline regression that a fresh checkout adopts the whole stale pre-attribution backlog (F5). The agent fixed F5 only on the Stale arm and kept 'a fresh public hold is yours'. That produced a doc drift in round 2 (F8), which was patched by reinforcing the same carve-out, and then round 3's F10, which proved the carve-out false and forced the Held-arm guard the reviewer had suggested in F5. F9 is an unrelated comment overclaim that the round-3 flag mis-attributes.
guidance_observations: The agent narrowed the reviewer's 'only match once minted' fix to one arm without checking which write paths can produce fresh unattributed evidence, and that check later settled F10 in a few lines.
The F3/F7 plans described a new self-identity type, but the landed fix deleted the branch; sibling threads replied minutes apart with different mechanisms for the same fix.
Fixing F8 by adding the freshness qualifier spread the incomplete F5 rule further instead of re-testing it, so the next round had to rewrite the same paragraph again.
